# t1.1 — Re-verify CSRF enforcement against a bootable application

## Result

Re-verified the restored Spring Security CSRF protection against both the full test suite and a packaged application running over HTTP. The repaired application starts, applies the additive `V2` migration, and enforces CSRF on live login, registration, and logout requests. No source or dependency changes were needed.

## Runtime Verification

- Packaged launch: `java -jar target/medicare-ai-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar --server.port=18080`
- Startup: PASS on Java 25.0.4.1 / Spring Boot 4.1.2; log reported `Started MediCareAiApplication in 8.321 seconds`.
- Database startup: Flyway successfully applied the additive migration to H2 schema `PUBLIC`, reaching version `v2`.
- Readiness: `GET /login` returned HTTP 200 and rendered a hidden `_csrf` input.
- Live requests (same cookie-backed browser session):
  - `POST /login` without a token → 403; with the login page token and valid credentials → 302 to `/dashboard`.
  - `POST /register` without a token → 403; with the page token and valid registration → 302 to `/login`.
  - `POST /logout` without a token → 403; with a fresh post-authentication token → 302 to `/login?logout`.
- Spring Security invalidates/refreshes the session CSRF token on successful authentication; the logout check fetched a fresh token after login. Reusing the pre-authentication token was correctly rejected.
- The packaged process was stopped after probing; port 18080 was confirmed no longer listening.
